The company reports more than 1.5 billion lifetime picks across robots fielded in 15 countries, with additional offices in Eindhoven (Netherlands) and Boulder, Colorado. Plus One Robotics publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; product integration is handled through its partner channel and a login-gated partner portal.

providers.name: Proactis
providers.description: Proactis provides procurement and spend management solutions including purchase-to-pay, e-sourcing, contract management, and spend analytics software for organizations.

providers.name: Redwood Materials
providers.description: Redwood Materials is a Carson City, Nevada battery materials company founded in 2017 by former Tesla CTO JB Straubel. It operates a domestic circular supply chain for lithium-ion batteries: collecting and recycling end-of-life EV, consumer, micromobility and stationary-storage batteries, refining the recovered lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper, and remanufacturing anode copper foil and cathode active material for North American cell producers. Through Redwood Energy it also deploys second-life battery energy storage systems for data centers and the grid. Redwood runs the Tahoe Campus in Northern Nevada, the Carolina Campus outside Charleston, South Carolina, and an R&D center in San Francisco, and works with Panasonic, Toyota, GM, BMW, VW/Audi, Rivian, Caterpillar, Isuzu and Lime. Redwood publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK or MCP server; its only machine-facing surface is a gated AWS Cognito partner portal used by automotive dismantlers to price and sell end-of-life battery packs.

providers.name: Stockly
providers.description: Stockly (Stockly SAS, headquartered in Vitry-sur-Seine, France) operates a global inventory network for e-commerce, positioning itself as "the first global inventory for Retail." It connects online retailers that are missing stock (Demanders) with brands and official retailers that hold surplus inventory (Suppliers), detecting out-of-stock variants and filling the gaps in real time so that e-shops never run out of stock. Stockly integrates directly with a retailer's e-commerce infrastructure via API, a CMS, or a marketplace, and is building toward a stock exchange for e-commerce inventory in compliance with brands' distribution policies. The company reports 300+ partnered retailers across Europe and 100M+ available items, and is backed by Techstars. Stockly is primarily a partner-onboarded platform rather than a broad self-serve public developer API.

providers.name: Another
providers.description: Another is an AI-native software platform that modernizes off-channel and off-price inventory operations for fashion, beauty, and retail brands. Founded in 2024 by Corina Marshall, the platform connects to a retailer's existing systems - including returns management - to create a single source of truth for excess, returned, and pre-loved goods, then automates how brands identify, manage, and monetize that inventory across downstream channels. Teams can invite and connect with secondary merchandise recipients, send inventory proposals to buyers, request payment from partners, and let partners request inventory, replacing fragmented manual workflows spread across teams, buyers, channels, and partners. Another closed a $2.5M seed round in January 2026 co-led by Anthemis and Westbound. As of this profile the company operates a private, invite-based web application and publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Dianxiaomi
providers.description: Dianxiaomi (店小秘) is a free cross-border e-commerce ERP platform operated by Shenzhen Meiyunji Network Technology Co., Ltd., serving more than 1.8 million cross-border sellers worldwide. It unifies product listing and data collection, multi-platform order processing, warehouse and inventory management, procurement, financial and profit analytics, and customer service across 70+ marketplaces including AliExpress, Amazon, Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop, with integrations to 1,700+ logistics providers and 130+ overseas warehouses. The platform is user-facing SaaS; no public developer/API open platform is currently published.

providers.name: EcomExperts
providers.description: EcomExperts is a Latin American ecommerce ERP and technology platform that helps online sellers manage, synchronize, and automate their stores from a single screen. It centralizes omnichannel operations across marketplaces and sales channels (including multi-account Mercado Libre management), synchronizes prices and stock in real time, and issues electronic invoices automatically in bulk. Delivered as a SaaS application with a hosted dashboard and a 7-day free trial, EcomExperts operates across Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Uruguay, Colombia, and Peru. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. EcomExperts does not currently publish a public developer platform, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures company identity and public-surface signals only.

providers.name: Fazla Gida
providers.description: Fazla (formerly Fazla Gida / Whole Surplus) is a Turkish technology-driven waste management and circular-economy company founded in 2017 in Istanbul. Its digital, decision-support platform helps B2B clients across the supply chain — manufacturers, retailers, e-commerce, distributors, HoReCa, food banks and municipalities — prevent waste at the source and recover value from surplus inventory through a food-recovery hierarchy of secondary-sales marketplace, donation, animal-feed conversion and recycling modules, backed by logistics support, a smart-scale IoT inventory system and an AI analysis tool that reports financial, CO2 and social impact. The company operates the Fazla Iyi surprise-box consumer app, is the first B Corp-certified waste-management organization in Turkey, and is backed by 500 Global among other investors.

providers.name: Fleetline
providers.description: Fleetline is an all-in-one AI dispatch and fleet-optimization platform for trucking fleets. Its AI-based dispatch engine ingests load, driver, and ELD data, simulates billions of scenarios, and recommends the best assignment plan so operators maximize revenue, productivity, and fleet utilization. The platform aggregates major load boards into a unified workspace, identifies schedule gaps and fills them with spot loads, composes complex trips with tradeoff analysis, forecasts delays, breakdowns, and HOS violations, and includes an AI assistant trained on fleet history and TMS data. Fleetline is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it exposes a marketing site, a customer login/auth portal, and an internal API host, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Forum Mobility
providers.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Omnifold
providers.description: Omnifold is an AI supply chain planning platform for physical product companies — CPGs, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers. The company trains a custom AI model for each supply chain to forecast demand, optimize inventory, and surface revenue, margin, and cash that traditional planning systems miss, positioning itself in the Forbes "Purpose-Built AI" tier and competing with Kinaxis, Blue Yonder, and o9. Omnifold was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Omnifold publishes marketing and product content but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or authentication surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Stellapps
providers.description: Stellapps is an end-to-end dairy technology company from Bangalore, India (IIT Madras incubated, founded 2011) that digitizes milk production, milk procurement, and cold-chain management through its SmartMoo full-stack IoT platform. Sensors in milking systems, animal wearables, chilling equipment, and procurement peripherals stream data to the SmartMoo Big Data Cloud for analytics and machine learning serving dairy farmers, cooperatives, and processors, with applications including mooON herd management, smartAMCU and smartCC milk procurement, ConTrak cold-chain monitoring, mooFlow ERP, and mooPay financial services. Stellapps publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; the SmartMoo platform is accessed through hosted applications behind CAS single sign-on.

providers.name: AutoZone
providers.description: AutoZone is the nation's leading retailer and a leading distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories with more than 7,000 stores across the Americas. AutoZone serves both do-it-yourself (DIY) customers and professional automotive service providers (DIFM) through retail stores, e-commerce, and electronic ordering integrations for commercial accounts via AutoZone Pro.

providers.name: Buildertrend
providers.description: Buildertrend is an Omaha, Nebraska-based cloud construction-management platform serving residential home builders, remodelers, and specialty trade contractors. The product consolidates sales (CRM, leads, proposals, contracts, email marketing), project management (schedule, daily logs, selections, change orders, warranties, sub portal, client updates), and financial management (estimates, bids, takeoff, job-costing budgets, bills, purchase orders, invoices, online payments) into a single web and mobile application used by 20,000+ builders. Pricing is custom-quoted by sales rather than published self-serve tiers, with unlimited users and projects on every plan, and the platform integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, and other accounting and trade tools through a partner integrations marketplace. The company exposes a REST API at api.buildertrend.com that is gated by partner agreement — endpoints return 401 Unauthorized to the public and there is no open developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API key signup. As a result Buildertrend is profiled here as a non-public (partner-only) API provider; the public surface documented is limited to marketing, support, integrations marketplace, mobile apps, and corporate resources.

providers.name: CF Industries Holdings
providers.description: CF Industries Holdings is a Fortune 500 American manufacturer and distributor of nitrogen-based fertilizers (ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, UAN) and clean-energy products serving agricultural and industrial customers worldwide. CF operates one of the largest global ammonia production networks and is scaling clean (blue and green) ammonia for low-carbon energy. CF does not publish a public developer API program; programmatic data access is limited to investor-relations SEC filings feeds, press/news RSS, and partner EDI/B2B integrations with agricultural distributors, rail, terminal, and industrial customers.

providers.name: Nuvocargo
providers.description: Nuvocargo is an AI-powered freight-management platform for North American truckload logistics, focused on the US-Mexico-Canada cross-border corridor. Its "Nuvo AI" system coordinates a network of specialized agents (quoting, negotiation, booking, dispatch, tracking, exception handling, audit, and payment) to automate the freight load lifecycle, and it pairs that software with licensed freight brokerage, managed transportation, and customs-brokerage services. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Homebrew and QED Investors. As of this enrichment pass Nuvocargo publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; onboarding is contact-gated ("zero-integration" pilots), so this profile captures the company identity, legal/resource surface, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Sensefinity
providers.description: Sensefinity is a supply-chain IoT company ("The IoT Transformation Company") delivering real-time tracking, monitoring, and analytics for global cargo and logistics operations. Its platform combines GPS/NB-IoT tracking devices for maritime containers, pallets, and vehicles with temperature and condition (cold-chain) sensors, indoor location tracking, a cloud analytics and machine learning layer, and digital product passport / blockchain integrations. The operational platform is delivered as a hosted web application (uiadmin.sensefinity.com) and mobile asset-management apps, serving enterprise customers across food, pharma, automotive, and manufacturing supply chains. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published as of this profile; a private API host (api.sensefinity.com) backs the platform.

providers.name: Reindeer AI
providers.description: Reindeer AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform that automates back-office business operations across finance, banking, insurance, supply chain, procurement, legal compliance, and global business services. Founded in 2024 with offices in New York and Tel Aviv, Reindeer deploys custom AI agents that learn from operational workflows using its Fast Track Training approach (functional models in roughly two weeks from a small number of samples), with human-in-the-loop escalation, continuous learning, and Model Reality Grounding safeguards against hallucination. It ships 200+ pre-trained skills and 200+ out-of-the-box integrations into systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, ServiceNow, and Salesforce, is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Bedrock, DeepSeek, GLM), and emphasizes customer data ownership and enterprise security (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 2, GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA). Reindeer is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, TEAM8, and Vesey Ventures. Reindeer does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal; the product is delivered as an enterprise engagement, so this profile captures company identity and security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: AptDeco
providers.description: AptDeco is a full-service online marketplace for buying and selling used, new, and vintage furniture. Founded in 2014 in New York City by Reham Fagiri and Kalam Dennis, the company handles the entire resale transaction end to end: pickup, disassembly and assembly, delivery, payment, scheduling, and logistics are all carried out by its own trained delivery teams. AptDeco serves the New York City metro, New Jersey, Connecticut, Philadelphia, Delaware, and the San Francisco Bay Area, and has expanded to additional US metros with national shipping. Backed by Y Combinator and Initialized Capital. AptDeco does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and developer surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flyzipline
providers.description: Flyzipline (Zipline International Inc., flyzipline.com / zipline.com) designs, manufactures, and operates autonomous delivery drones for food, groceries, and medicine. Its instant logistics platform flies vital shipments — blood products, vaccines, pharmaceuticals, prepared meals, and retail goods — on direct aerial routes at up to 70 mph, with temperature-controlled pods and real-time tracking. Zipline operates distribution centers across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan, partnering with health systems, retailers (Walmart, Chipotle), and restaurant technology providers (Olo) that submit delivery requests through Zipline's ordering system or software integrations. As of early 2026 the fleet has completed more than two million commercial deliveries across 120+ million autonomous miles. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-adjacent portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Zipline publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time — partner integrations are bespoke.

providers.name: Parlevel
providers.description: Parlevel Systems is a San Antonio-based vending technology company (founded 2012, now part of 365 Retail Markets) providing a Vending Management System (VMS) and related tools for unattended retail operators across vending, micro markets, and office coffee service. The platform covers real-time machine telemetry, dynamic route optimization, cashless payments (PayPlus), inventory and warehouse management, and cash accountability. No public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or documented webhook surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Shippingbo
providers.description: Shippingbo is a Toulouse, France-based e-commerce logistics SaaS founded in 2016 by Marc Hericher and Romain Parent. The platform unifies an Order Management System (OMS), Warehouse Management System (WMS), and Transport Management System (TMS) behind a single REST API so that merchants, DNVBs, 3PLs, wholesalers, manufacturers, and marketplaces can centralize multi-channel orders, pilot warehouse picking and packing, and execute multi-carrier shipments from one back office. Shippingbo claims 5,000+ active users, 80 million orders, and EUR 5 billion in merchandise handled in 2024, with 2,500+ warehouses equipped across France and Europe. The Shippingbo Developer Portal (powered by Stoplight) exposes a public REST/JSON API covering orders, products, stocks, shipments, customers, pickings, and source connectors, secured by OAuth 2.0 through the oauth.shippingbo.com authorization server. Shippingbo additionally offers a dedicated TMS API for multi-carrier label generation and a webhook channel for order state changes, stock changes, and shipment events. Reported developer-facing scale includes 500+ developers, 10+ million orders processed through the APIs, 500+ million webhook deliveries, and 40+ pre-integrated carriers. Shippingbo is a French Tech company backed by IRDI Capital Investissement and GSO Innovation.

providers.name: Tengo
providers.description: Tengo is an AI-powered public procurement platform that helps companies find, evaluate, and respond to public tenders in one place. Founded in 2023 in France by Hugues Renou and Yoann Gauthier, Tengo covers the full tender lifecycle — sourcing and targeting relevant opportunities, drafting and writing proposals with AI, and managing responses and performance analytics — serving SMEs, mid-sized companies, and large corporations. Tengo raised a €3M round led by Point Nine in 2024. It operates a business-user SaaS with a request-a-demo onboarding and no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Bounce
providers.description: Bounce operates the world's largest luggage storage network, connecting travelers with more than 32,000 vetted partner locations across 4,000+ cities worldwide where they can securely drop off bags, luggage, and packages by the hour or day and explore hands-free. Founded by Cody Candee in 2018, the company runs a two-sided marketplace: travelers book storage in advance or on the spot through the Bounce web and mobile apps, while local shops, hotels, and businesses earn revenue as storage partners. Bounce also offers luggage-delivery between hotels, airports, and city locations, a hotel solutions program, and an affiliate program. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, and Sapphire. This profile currently tracks the company's public web surface; Bounce publishes an llms.txt but no public developer API.

providers.name: Dagangan
providers.description: Dagangan is an Indonesian tech-enabled wholesale e-commerce platform serving small and medium retailers (SMEs) in tier 3-4 cities and rural areas. Through a hub-and-spoke network of 50+ micro-warehouses across remote regions, it connects large suppliers to traditional local retailers, giving them affordable mobile access to daily necessities and groceries while reducing delivery costs and supply-chain friction. The company operates a consumer/retailer Android shopping application (Dagangan Mall), is backed by 500 Global, and is recognized as a Rural Digitalization Partner of Indonesia's Ministry of Villages, Disadvantaged Regions, and Transmigration. As of this profile, Dagangan publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Donkey
providers.description: Donkey is an AI-native trading company (Y Combinator, Summer 2026) that buys directly from Chinese factories and sells delivered duty-paid to US importers. Donkey mines public US customs records to identify the factory that actually makes a product, returns a landed DDP quote within 72 hours, runs its own on-the-floor quality inspections before the factory is paid, clears customs, moves the money, and offers credit-insured net-45 terms to qualified buyers. Founded by Benjamin Martindale (CEO) and Minghao Tan (CTO), the company runs small teams in San Francisco and China. Donkey publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform today; this profile tracks its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kodiak Robotics
providers.description: Kodiak Robotics, which now operates publicly as Kodiak AI, is an autonomous vehicle company founded in April 2018 by CEO Don Burnette and headquartered in California with a Texas operations center. Its flagship product is the Kodiak Driver, an AI-driven autonomy system that pairs onboard artificial intelligence with modular, swappable sensor hardware and offboard services so that a single driverless stack can be carried across different vehicle platforms. The company sells into three markets — long-haul trucking, defense, and industrial ground transportation — and positions driverless operation as a safety improvement, citing that more than 85% of U.S. truck crashes are caused by human error. Kodiak reports more than 2.6 million autonomous miles driven and over 7,000 loads delivered. Kodiak publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs; enrichment probes of kodiak.ai found no /.well-known/ discovery documents and no api/docs/developer subdomains. It does publish an llms.txt, an RSS news feed, and a corporate safety report, so this profile is maintained as a company record rather than an API producer profile.

providers.name: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd. (주식회사 곳간, branded KOKKAN / 도심창고 곳간) is a South Korean urban self-storage and logistics operator headquartered in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. It rents managed storage units in five sizes (S, M, L, XL, XXL, from 1.0m cubes up to 2.0 x 2.0 x 2.0m) across 22 branches in Seoul, Busan, Incheon, Gyeonggi and Chungbuk, serving households storing seasonal appliances, clothing, bedding and baby goods as well as businesses storing samples, inventory, documents and office equipment. Customers select a branch, choose a unit size, pay and manage their contract through the KOKKAN mobile apps for iOS and Android, with recurring monthly card billing through a Korean payment gateway, long-term and promotional discounting, an address-rental (주소지 임대) product, and an optional pickup service for moving stored goods. The company also runs a franchise and partnership program for operators who want to open a KOKKAN branch. It was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this profile KokkanLogis publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or technical documentation — the product surface is a consumer website plus native mobile apps.

providers.name: Salasa
providers.description: Salasa is an end-to-end eCommerce logistics provider based in Saudi Arabia, offering 3PL fulfillment (warehouse storage, automated pick/pack/ship), hyperlocal dark stores with 2-hour delivery in Riyadh, domestic on-demand and scheduled shipping, cross-border shipping with customs clearance, and reverse logistics / return management. Its Operations Management System (OMS) provides real-time tracking, inventory management, and analytics, and it connects to major eCommerce platforms (Salla, Zid, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, Amazon, Trendyol) and offers custom API integrations for merchants automating fulfillment and order synchronization.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel (Apeel Sciences) is a food technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Goleta, California. It produces a plant-derived, edible coating, made from lipids and glycerolipids found in the peels, seeds and pulp of produce, that is applied to fresh fruit and vegetables at packing houses to slow water loss and oxidation, extending shelf life and reducing food waste across the supply chain. Apeel-treated produce is sold through grocery retailers in multiple countries. In 2021 Apeel acquired ImpactVision and added hyperspectral imaging to its supplier installations to grade interior quality, ripeness and freshness. Apeel is a materials-science and supply-chain operator: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer sign-up.

providers.name: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings
providers.description: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings is a global airfreight, charter, and aircraft leasing group headquartered in Purchase, New York and operating across more than 80 countries and 330+ airports. The holding company positions itself as the "Leader in Aviation Outsourcing" and runs three operating businesses: Atlas Air (ACMI, CMI, charter, and military/government cargo and passenger operations on Boeing 747-400F, 747-8F, 777F, 767, and 737-800BCF freighters), Polar Air Cargo (scheduled airport-to-airport cargo network, historically a joint venture with DHL), and Titan Aviation Leasing (commercial aircraft acquisition, leasing, and sale-leaseback services). Atlas is the largest operator of the Boeing 747 freighter, the Dreamlifter operator for Boeing, and one of the principal lift providers for Amazon Air's middle-mile network. In August 2022 a consortium led by Apollo Global Management with J.F. Lehman & Company and Hill City Capital agreed to take the company private in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately US$5.2 billion; the deal closed in March 2023, delisting the company (formerly Nasdaq: AAWW). As a freight carrier the group does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs — integrations with shippers, forwarders, and customers are delivered through private B2B channels (EDI, Cargo-IMP/XML messaging, airwaybill tracking on polaraircargo.com, and account-managed connectivity). A "Track Shipment" tool and a Special Loads request form (specialloads.atlasair.com) are the principal self-service surfaces; an internal-facing GitHub organization (Atlas-Air-Data-Platform) exists but publishes no public repos.

providers.name: Catena-X
providers.description: Catena-X is the automotive industry's data space standard, published by Catena-X Automotive Network e.V. — a non-commercial German registered association founded on 15 May 2021 by BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, Bosch, SAP, Siemens, Schaeffler, ZF, BASF, Henkel, Deutsche Telekom and Fraunhofer, with backing from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action. It publishes a numbered CX-xxxx library of 77 standards covering how a supply chain exchanges part data, carbon footprints, quality records, demand and capacity signals and digital product passports without any participant surrendering its data to a central platform. Standards move forward together in named releases — Jupiter, Io, Saturn, Titan — gated by a Technical Committee for Standardization, and conformance is certified by nominated third-party assessment bodies including TÜV Rheinland and TÜV SÜD. The reference implementation is open source as Eclipse Tractus-X, and the network is operated commercially by Cofinity-X. It is the most institutionally complete industry API standard in Europe, and the one whose endpoints an outside developer can never call: in a data space every participant runs its own connector and registry, so there is nothing to call until you are onboarded, credentialed and certified.

providers.name: Chord
providers.description: Chord is a New York / Santa Barbara-based commerce data and AI platform founded in 2021 by Bryan Mahoney (CEO) and Henry Davis (President & Chairman), both former Glossier executives. Chord began as a headless commerce backbone built on top of Solidus — the open-source Spree Commerce fork written in Ruby on Rails — and has since evolved into an AI-native commerce data platform with three layers: a Data Foundation that unifies sources such as Shopify, ad platforms, and CDPs; a Context Stack that grounds AI in store-specific business context; and a set of Agents that take action across the commerce stack. Its current product surface includes Chord OMS (a Solidus-based order management system covering orders, products, promotions, subscriptions, affiliates, gift cards, returns, shipping, tax, and digital products documented at chord.stoplight.io), Chord CDP (customer data platform with identity resolution, RFM scoring, customer lifetime revenue, and destination activations), Chord Event Tracking (client- and server-side eventing with Shopify Web Pixel integration and consent management via OneTrust and Shopify Customer Privacy API), Chord Data Platform (analytics, predictive modeling, attribution, recommendations, Fivetran ingestion, GA4 compatibility), and Chord AI / Copilot Chat, powered by Anthropic Claude (Opus 4.5 for SQL generation, Haiku 4.5 for response generation and classification) with charts, monitors, context modeling, and natural-language data querying. Chord's GitHub org (github.com/chordcommerce) maintains a fleet of Solidus extensions (solidus_stripe, solidus_braintree, solidus_paypal_braintree, solidus_subscriptions, solidus_virtual_gift_card, solidus_importer, solidus_avatax_certified), a consent-manager TypeScript library, a Jitsu fork for event ingestion, and example repos for eventing and analytics. Notable customers include Sonos, Blue Bottle Coffee, Rodan + Fields, MrBeast, and Ritual. Funding has come from M13 Ventures, Equal Ventures, Act One Ventures, Chingona Ventures, and CEAS Investments, with an $18M Series A reported by TechCrunch in 2021. The commercial model is sales-led with custom enterprise pricing gated behind a demo request.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: Focal Systems
providers.description: Focal Systems is a San Francisco-based deep-learning company building the operating system for brick-and-mortar retail. Its platform combines proprietary shelf-mounted computer-vision cameras, real-time AI, and streaming data to digitize physical stores hourly — tracking on-shelf availability, out-of-stocks, planogram and price-tag compliance, shrink, and inventory. Products include Computer Vision cameras, Shelf AI, the Action Tool associate mobile app, and the Impact analytics dashboard, used by leading grocery and retail chains such as Walmart Canada to reduce waste, redeploy labor, and recover lost sales. Focal Systems is a Y Combinator and Uncork Capital-backed company and operates as an enterprise SaaS vendor; it does not publish a public self-serve developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Indrive
providers.description: inDrive is a global ride-hailing, delivery, and urban-services platform built around a peer-to-peer, name-your-price model in which passengers propose a fare and nearby drivers accept, counter, or decline it directly. Founded in 2012 by Arsen Tomsky in Yakutsk, Russia and now headquartered in Mountain View, California, the company operates across roughly 48 countries and more than 1,000 cities, with over 400 million app downloads. Beyond city rides it offers intercity transport, courier and freight delivery, on-demand task services, and driver lending. inDrive was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and General Catalyst. inDrive does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; its GitHub organization hosts internal engineering frameworks and an engineering handbook rather than external API definitions.

providers.name: Tezbor, Inc.
providers.description: Tezbor is a Tashkent, Uzbekistan based courier and last-mile logistics company that automates the delivery of documents, parcels, and cargo across Uzbekistan. Beyond its consumer and business courier service, Tezbor operates a technology platform that exposes delivery ordering and tracking through an integration API, ready-made e-commerce plugins (WooCommerce, OpenCart, Magento), mobile apps, dashboards, and Telegram bots, so that any online store can automatically generate a Tezbor delivery order from each purchase. The company is backed by 500 Global, Activat, and StartupBase, and counts brands such as Beeline, Ozon, and OQ among its delivery clients.

providers.name: Deppon Express
providers.description: Deppon Express (德邦快递), operated by Deppon Logistics Co., Ltd., is a major Chinese express delivery and logistics provider specializing in large-parcel (heavy/bulky) express, less-than-truckload freight, full-truckload, air freight, warehousing, supply chain, and cross-border services. Founded from Cui's Freight Company (1996) and incorporated in 2009, it became part of the JD Logistics group in 2022 and ranks among China's largest express carriers by market share. For developers and enterprise partners, Deppon runs the Deppon Open Platform (德邦开放平台, established 2015) at dpopen.deppon.com, offering system-integration APIs for order creation, standard track/tracking queries, and electronic waybill (面单) printing, with access granted to contracted monthly-settlement customers.

providers.name: Woowa Brothers
providers.description: Woowa Brothers is the Seoul-based technology company behind Baedal Minjok (Baemin), South Korea's leading food delivery platform, alongside B-Mart quick commerce, Baemin Connect rider services, and robotics initiatives for serving and delivery robots. A subsidiary of Delivery Hero since 2021, the company runs a strong engineering culture through its Woowahan tech blog and first-party open-source libraries on GitHub (NestJS libraries, WoowahanJS, Redis tooling), but it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Blau Corp
providers.description: Blau (Blau Corp) is a waste-management operating system for haulers (gestores), final-destination facilities, and government regulators across Mexico, Colombia, and Spain. The SaaS platform delivers AI-assisted route optimization, route-level profitability analysis, automated RP and RPBI hazardous- and biological-infectious-waste manifests, online collection booking, and end-to-end traceability, plus the Blau Driver mobile app for field crews. Founded in Guadalajara, Mexico in 2021 and backed by 500 Global (LatAm B17 batch), Blau integrates with SAT/CFDI, SEMARNAT, SAP/ERP, QuickBooks, WhatsApp, fleet GPS, and Power BI. Blau does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: FlagshipRTL
providers.description: FlagshipRTL (Flagship) is a SaaS company providing AI-powered inventory forecasting and merchandise planning software for retail brands, with a focus on apparel and direct-to-consumer (DTC) businesses. Its platform pairs demand forecasting at size-level granularity with multi-scenario planning, a purchase-order (PO) builder, and real-time inventory alerts to help retailers reduce stockouts and maximize full-price sell-through. Flagship reports optimizing over $2B in GMV for customers such as Bala, Mack Weldon, and Fresh Clean Threads, and integrates with systems including Shopify, NetSuite, Cin7, Snowflake, and Google Sheets. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Focal Point Procurement Solutions
providers.description: Focal Point is an AI-powered procurement orchestration platform for enterprise procurement teams. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the SaaS platform sits on top of a company's existing S2P and ERP systems to centralize procurement data, intake, and workflows across six core modules: Request Intake Management, Procurement Activity Management, Sourcing Event Management, Supplier Relationship Management, Third-Party Risk Management, and Contract Lifecycle Management. It connects existing systems and data via API integrations, automates tactical no-code workflows, and provides total spend visibility, intelligent intake, and smart routing so procurement teams can focus on strategic work. Focal Point does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal; integrations are delivered through the platform. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jingle
providers.description: Jingle is a consumer marketplace mobile app for fast, direct local deliveries from mobile stores and services — "shops-on-wheels" — operating in the San Francisco Bay Area. Users sign up with a phone number (no password) and enable push notifications to be alerted when their favorite mobile vendors are nearby — artisanal food trucks, farmers'-market sellers, and one-click services such as bike repair, car wash, manicures, pedicures, and knife sharpening — then request a "jingle" to summon them. Deliveries are handled directly by the businesses themselves, cutting out delivery middlemen. Merchants use the app at their discretion to broadcast their presence to nearby neighborhoods, and residential complexes can partner to bring vendors on-site. Jingle is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its public consumer and merchant surface.

providers.name: Open Port Technology
providers.description: Open Port Technology (OpenPort) is a pan-Asian logistics and supply chain technology company that digitizes trucking, freight, and supply chain operations across emerging markets through an open, neutral, AI-based platform. Headquartered in Karachi, Pakistan, its product suite spans transport management (OpenTM), a digital trucking marketplace (OpenMarket), customs clearance (OpenClear), warehouse picking operations (OpenPick), and FBR digital invoicing (Open Invoice). The company reports millions of completed shipments, 1,600+ transport partners, and integrations across 100+ ERP systems, offering ERP integration and custom API development to clients, though it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: TradeLink
providers.description: TradeLink is a Munich-based logistics SaaS company building the first collaboration platform for supply chain and inbound/outbound logistics. Its cloud software gives warehouses, suppliers, carriers, and dispatchers a shared system for time-slot (dock) booking, dock and yard management, load-carrier and empties management, driver check-in terminals, and analytics insights, replacing phone and email coordination with real-time, transparent workflows. TradeLink integrates with existing ERP and transport-management systems and serves production, retail, and contract-logistics companies across the DACH region and Europe, with customers including MAN, SPAR, Liebherr, and Emons. It is backed by Insight Partners and Point Nine.

providers.name: Venwiz
providers.description: Venwiz is a Bengaluru, India based B2B digital platform for the procurement of industrial and infrastructural project services, covering both CapEx and MRO requirements for the manufacturing sector. Founded in 2020 by Rajesh Reddy and Sandesh Paturi, it operates a marketplace that connects industrial buyers with a verified, pan-India database of service vendors, adding vendor discovery, order expediting, project management tooling and vendor intelligence on top. Backed by Accel and other investors (~$11.4M raised), Venwiz digitises what has traditionally been an offline, relationship-driven industrial services procurement process. No public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this enrichment pass; the public presence is a marketing/content website plus a login-gated application.

providers.name: Afresh Technologies
providers.description: Afresh Technologies builds an AI platform for grocery retail that helps supermarkets and distributors manage fresh food, reducing shrink, improving in-stock rates, and cutting food waste across store ordering, inventory management, production planning, recipe management, and distribution-center buying. Its machine-learning decision engine forecasts demand for perishable, random-weight, and bulk items where operational data is inherently messy, and is also offered as a backend Replenishment API that plugs Afresh's forecasting and ordering logic into a retailer's existing front-end systems without changing in-store associate workflows. The company is based in San Francisco and is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Dronamics
providers.description: Dronamics is a European deep-tech company that designs, builds, and operates autonomous long-range cargo drones for middle-mile logistics. Its flagship aircraft, The Black Swan, is a remotely piloted UAV that carries up to 350 kg (770 lb) of cargo over distances up to 2,500 km (1,550 mi), enabling same-day, cross-border, point-to-point deliveries that are faster, cheaper, and lower in CO2 emissions than traditional air freight. Founded in 2014 in Sofia, Bulgaria by brothers Svilen and Konstantin Rangelov and operating as Dronamics Group Limited, the company is building the world's first cargo drone airline, operating a proprietary drone fleet from a network of low-cost droneports. The public dronamics.com marketing site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access; Dronamics does not publish a developer-facing logistics API, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: KWI
providers.description: KWI is a retail technology company founded in 1985 and headquartered in Melville, New York, that delivers a cloud-based, unified commerce platform for specialty and department retailers. The platform combines an iOS mobile point-of-sale, merchandising and inventory optimization, order management with buy-anywhere / fulfill-from-anywhere fulfillment, CRM, clienteling and loyalty, the Snapshot real-time sales analytics application, and AI product image search, all operated as a SaaS managed service with helpdesk, hardware, and payments support. KWI describes an API layer in its platform architecture used to export data to third-party systems and channels --- CRMs, ERPs, SRPs, and supply chains --- alongside packaged connectors such as Shopify Connect and a Klaviyo connector. As of this profile KWI publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, or SDKs; integration is delivered through its professional-services organization under customer contract.

providers.name: blueflite
providers.description: blueflite is a Techstars-backed unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) company that designs and manufactures autonomous cargo and delivery drones built on its SLATE platform for all-weather, time-sensitive logistics. Its aircraft target last-mile shipping and medical or life-saving delivery (such as defibrillators and emergency supplies), and the company complements the hardware with blueDelivery (a consumer ordering app), blueDigital (a cloud productivity tool), and blueControl, alongside drone consulting, engineering, and project services. blueflite is on the FAA Section 44807 approved UAS list and holds FCC conditional approval, and was founded by Frank Noppel and James McClearen. No public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Good Eggs
providers.description: Good Eggs is an online grocery marketplace founded in 2011 that delivers "absurdly fresh" groceries, meal kits, and locally sourced food to homes across the West Coast of the United States, primarily the San Francisco Bay Area and Southern California. The company curates a marketplace of over 6,000 items from local farms, ranches, fisheries, and independent food makers, and operates its own fulfillment and same-day/next-day delivery logistics. Good Eggs is a consumer-facing e-commerce and delivery business; it maintains a verified public GitHub organization for its engineering open-source and internal tooling but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (GV, Index Ventures, Obvious Ventures) and enriched with the company's real public web properties.

providers.name: Koobz
providers.description: Koobz is a Ventura, California additive-manufacturing company rebuilding the footwear supply chain around on-demand 3D printing. Its "gigafactory" prints circular-ready, mono-material foamed-TPU shoes to order, so brands carry zero inventory and face no minimum order quantities: a consumer buys on the brand's own storefront, the order and personalization specs sync to the Koobz factory, the shoe is printed in Ventura and dropshipped direct to the customer in days. The company markets 10x faster concept-to-market cycles (4-6 weeks, no tooling), custom cushioning and foot-scanning personalization, and a KoobzWeave toolpath-as-textile upper pattern engine. Its mono-material architecture is positioned for Extended Producer Responsibility regimes such as California SB 707, since a single-polymer shoe yields premium TPU on take-back rather than mixed waste. Koobz has raised $7.2M and is backed by Uncork Capital. It describes its factory as API-driven and its order intake as an API sync from brand storefronts, but as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition; integration appears to run through its partner ("Partner With Us") channel.

providers.name: MedArrive
providers.description: MedArrive is a healthcare technology company that provides a logistics and workforce platform for in-home care delivery. Its software gives health systems and in-home care providers smart scheduling, real-time provider routing, automated re-routing and patient reminders, and a live command-center dashboard for tracking every provider and visit, alongside a provider mobile app for field teams. The HIPAA-compliant platform is designed to reduce windshield time, cut scheduling effort, and increase daily visit capacity so care teams spend more time with patients and less on logistics. MedArrive is backed by Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Reibus
providers.description: Reibus is a technology-enabled B2B platform for the industrial metals industry, originally a digital marketplace for buying and selling steel and other metals and now focused on open-deck freight logistics for shipping steel and industrial metals. Operating as Reibus Logistics, the company connects shippers with a vast network of international and domestic carriers across flatbed, dry van, and drayage modes, offering instant quoting, shipment visibility, and cross-border logistics in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Founded by CEO John Blount, Reibus operates in 7 countries, does business in 25+ countries, and is backed by Canaan Partners, Initialized Capital, and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Remedial Health
providers.description: Remedial Health is a Nigeria-based healthtech company digitizing pharmaceutical procurement and pharmacy operations across Africa. Its platform connects retail pharmacies, hospitals, clinics, health insurers/HMOs, and pharmaceutical manufacturers through a set of products: Remedial Store (a digital marketplace for pharmacies to procure inventory), Remedial RX (daily pharmacy operations and inventory tooling), Remedial Buy Now-Pay Later (inventory financing), the Remedial Benefits Manager (clinical pharmacy services and medication delivery for insurers), Remedial Market Access (distribution reach for manufacturers), and Remedial Intelligence (supply-chain data insights). The company is backed by QED Investors and reaches its customers primarily through Android and iOS mobile apps. As of this enrichment pass Remedial Health publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation host; this profile captures its identity, legal, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: RightHand Robotics
providers.description: RightHand Robotics builds autonomous piece-picking robotic systems for order fulfillment. Its RightPick platform combines computer vision, machine learning, and adaptive grasping hardware to pick and place millions of SKUs at cycle times as fast as three seconds across e-commerce, pharmaceutical, apparel, health & beauty, and grocery operations. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund. RightHand Robotics does not publish a public web API; integration, deployment, and operator documentation is provided to authorized customers and partners through a login-gated partner portal (rhrdocs.com). The public GitHub organization hosts open-source ROS packages and C control libraries for the earlier ReFlex robotic hand hardware rather than web-API client SDKs.

providers.name: AutoTrac
providers.description: AutoTrac is a Brazilian fleet management and vehicle tracking technology company with over 30 years of experience. As the national market leader, AutoTrac provides satellite and cellular fleet tracking solutions, real-time telemetry, driver journey management, and management intelligence platforms for logistics, agriculture, maritime, and insurance sectors. The company operates its own terrestrial satellite communication station and data center for nationwide coverage.

providers.name: Craftable
providers.description: Craftable is hospitality's back-office software platform for restaurants, bars, hotels, and resorts, originally known for its Bevager and Foodager products, that connects purchasing, inventory, recipes, and accounts payable with accounting and sales data. Its suite spans Intelligent Ordering (eProcurement), AP Automation with Invoice AI, Inventory and Recipe Management, and Daily Actionable Insights, plus AI features such as Operator AI and the Crafty in-app assistant. Craftable is SOC 2 compliant and SSO-capable, with more than 1,000 POS, EDI, and vendor/API integrations spanning systems such as Toast, Square, Lightspeed, Clover, SpotOn, TouchBistro, Aloha by NCR Voyix, Restaurant365, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, and Xero. Craftable does not publish a public self-service developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; integrations are delivered through its implementation team during onboarding, and API access to a connected platform is provisioned by requesting a scoped API key from that platform's support team.

providers.name: Elektrik App
providers.description: Elektrik is a medium voltage (MV) equipment procurement platform for electrical distributors, contractors, and Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms. Founded in 2020 by Mario Dealba out of the Techstars Alabama EnergyTech Accelerator, the company streamlines sourcing of medium- to high-voltage supplies (roughly 5kV-35kV / 600V-69kV) including MV cable, terminations, splices, deadbreak and loadbreak connectors, and transformers. Buyers build part lists and specifications in the web app and Elektrik surfaces matching products across leading manufacturers such as TE Connectivity, BURNDY, Richards Manufacturing, and PFISTERER, compressing a traditionally slow, quote-driven procurement cycle. Backed by Techstars and growth capital, Elektrik is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: NGL Energy Partners
providers.description: NGL Energy Partners LP is a diversified midstream master limited partnership providing transportation, storage, blending, and marketing services for crude oil, natural gas liquids, refined products, and water solutions to producers and end-users across the energy industry. The company is publicly traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol NGL and operates three primary business units: Crude Oil Logistics, Water Solutions, and NGL Liquids.

providers.name: Platformable
providers.description: Platformable provides API governance, open ecosystem intelligence, and consultancy services. Their training resources, dashboards, and tools help organizations build comprehensive, automated, high quality API governance systems and participate in open digital ecosystems including open banking, digital health, and traceability.

providers.name: Sprouts Farmers Market
providers.description: Sprouts Farmers Market is a specialty grocery retailer focused on fresh, natural, and organic foods at affordable prices. Operating primarily in the western United States, Sprouts integrates with third-party platforms including Instacart, DoorDash, and Uber Eats for online grocery delivery. Sprouts uses EDI-based supply chain integrations and participates in Instacart's AI-powered Cart Assistant program. There is no public developer API; integrations are handled through EDI and third-party delivery platform partnerships.

providers.name: USA Rare Earth
providers.description: USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) is an American critical-minerals and advanced-materials company building a domestic mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain. It operates a 310,000 sq. ft. sintered neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma, and holds the Round Top heavy rare earth and critical minerals deposit in Hudspeth County, West Texas. The company produces rare earth elements, oxides, metals and sintered permanent magnets for defense, automotive, robotics, industrial and clean-energy customers, with the stated aim of reducing U.S. dependence on offshore rare earth processing and magnet production. It is a materials producer and manufacturer, not a software or data company, and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: WESCO International
providers.description: WESCO International is a Fortune 500 leading provider of business-to-business distribution, logistics services, and supply chain solutions for electrical, industrial, communications, and utility customers worldwide. WESCO serves over 150,000 customers through a network of branches and distribution centers and provides comprehensive digital integration capabilities including EDI, punchout, cXML, and API connectivity for procurement automation.

providers.name: Freshop
providers.description: Freshop is an eCommerce platform purpose-built for grocery and specialty retail, now part of NCR Voyix. It powers branded online storefronts, mobile shopping, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery for independent and regional grocers, and integrates third-party services for loyalty, coupons, email, SMS, and fulfillment. Freshop exposes a live REST API at api.freshop.com that serves store and product data to Freshop-powered storefronts and apps, authenticated with an application key (app_key) query-string parameter and versioned by a numeric path segment.

providers.name: Kaizntree Inc.
providers.description: Kaizntree is a New York-based operations platform for growth-stage consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands, giving multi-channel manufacturers and sellers a single system to run purchasing, inventory, sales, fulfillment, production, and lot-level traceability. Its two products are Kaizntree OS, a cloud ERP that centralizes stock across raw materials, intermediate goods, packaging, finished and bundled products with COGS, margin, multi-location, batch/expiry and audit-ready records, and JP, an ERP-agnostic AI operations assistant that automates high-volume workflows such as purchase-order processing, reporting, data synchronization, and OTIF tracking. Kaizntree integrates with sales channels (including Shopify), accounting, WMS, and fulfillment platforms. Backed by 500 Global (seed, 2022), it operates on usage-based pricing. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Kaizntree publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Onramp Payments
providers.description: Onramp Payments, Inc. (ONRAMP) is a fintech company building modern payments infrastructure for the commercial trucking and fleet industry. Founded by logistics and payments veterans and backed by Canaan Partners, the company operates an enterprise-grade digital platform that replaces legacy card-based fleet payment systems. For carriers it offers cardless fuel payments at the pump, administrative spend controls, and maintenance payment solutions; for merchants it provides digital payment acceptance, pricing controls, and fraud prevention that work both in-store and at fuel pumps; and for partners it offers API integrations, broker solutions, and Transportation Management System (TMS) connections. The company markets itself as the easiest, most secure payments platform for carriers and merchants and has raised roughly $21M from investors including Canaan Partners, CEAS Investments, Contour Venture Partners, Javelin Venture Partners, and RedBlue Capital. As of this enrichment pass ONRAMP publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures verified company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: sherpa
providers.description: sherpa is an AI operating system for External Workforce Management (EWM) that runs an enterprise's contingent-labor program end to end with autonomous agents, replacing the work traditionally done by a VMS (Vendor Management System) and MSP (Managed Service Provider). Its agents cover every phase of an external engagement: autonomous intake and classification from Slack, email, Teams or voice; collaborative scope, role and budget drafting; autonomous sourcing with market-benchmarked rates and ranked candidates and suppliers; coordinated screening interviews scored against a weighted rubric; autonomous hiring and onboarding (documents, background and compliance checks, contracts, provisioning, hardware and badges); and active management and payment with a dedicated PM agent, live spend visibility and flexible payouts once outcomes are verified. One platform spans every worker type — contingent labor, freelancers / independent contractors (with a built-in Agent of Record), SOW / services engagements, and, coming soon, AI agents as a managed worker type — with rate intelligence, compliance management and analytics built in. sherpa launched out of stealth with a $2.2M pre-seed round and is backed by Seedcamp and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Swift Transportation
providers.description: Swift Transportation, now operating as Knight-Swift Transportation Holdings (KNX), is the largest full truckload motor carrier in North America. The company provides truckload, LTL, logistics, and intermodal transportation services across the US, Mexico, and Canada. Technology integration is primarily through EDI for freight tendering, shipment status, and invoicing workflows with trading partners and shippers.

providers.name: Universal Forest Products
providers.description: UFP Industries (formerly Universal Forest Products) is a leading global manufacturer and distributor of wood and wood-alternative products serving retail, industrial, and construction markets. UFP operates over 200 facilities globally supplying lumber, engineered wood products, packaging, and building materials. The company has integrated OnBase-based business system integration for document management and workflow automation across its supply chain operations.

providers.name: Advantive
providers.description: Advantive is an AI-enabled software company for specialty manufacturing and distribution operations, unifying ERP, MES, quality (SPC/SQC), PLM, WMS, and B2B commerce workflows into industry-specific systems. Built from a portfolio of brands including Advantzware, DDI System, Distribution One, InfinityQS (Enact and ProFicient), Kiwiplan, WinSPC, and VIA, Advantive serves more than 2,500 customers across eight countries in verticals such as food and beverage, packaging (corrugated, folding carton, plastics), automotive, aerospace and defense, electronics, and distribution of fasteners, bearings, HVAC, and janitorial supplies. The company is a private-equity-backed operations software provider; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public digital surface. No public developer API or OpenAPI has been found — integration is delivered through the products' own connectors and the Advantive support portal.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel Sciences is a food technology company headquartered in Santa Barbara, California that develops plant-based protective coatings which extend the shelf life of fresh fruits and vegetables. The company uses food-grade ingredients derived from the peels, pulp, and seeds of plants to create a thin, edible layer that reinforces produce's natural peel, slowing water loss and oxidation. This extends peak taste, juiciness, and nutrient retention while reducing reliance on refrigeration, waxes, pesticides, and plastic packaging across the fresh-produce supply chain. Apeel positions itself as a sustainability and food-waste leader, reporting that since 2021 its technology has prevented millions of pieces of fruit from spoiling, avoided tens of thousands of metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions, and conserved billions of liters of water. Its products have undergone regulatory review in the United States, European Union, and other markets. Apeel is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification as of this profile.

providers.name: autone
providers.description: autone is an AI-powered inventory management platform for retail brands, blending machine-driven recommendations with merchandising expertise and a brand's own data to optimize stock decisions across buying, reordering, replenishment, and rebalancing. Its modules — Buy, Reorder, Replenish, Rebalance, Assortment & Initial Allocation, and Insights — help fashion, beauty, furniture, and sports retailers reduce stockouts and overstock, redistribute inventory across locations, and improve margins. Founded by supply-chain operators from luxury fashion houses (Alexander McQueen, Victoria Beckham, Givenchy), autone is backed by General Catalyst, Seedcamp, and Speedinvest. No public developer API or documentation is published at this time; the platform is delivered as an enterprise SaaS. This profile originated as a VC-portfolio lead and has been enriched with verifiable company identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Clarium
providers.description: Clarium is a healthcare supply chain resiliency company founded in early 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and headquartered in New York City. Its AI-powered platform, Astra OS, unifies real-time data from hospitals and their suppliers across systems of record, then layers data-enabled workflow apps on top: Disruption Monitoring to detect and resolve supply chain disruptions faster, Substitute Management to automate product approvals, and Procedure Card Optimization to standardize and cut cost. Clarium has raised $43M+ (including a $27M Series A led by General Catalyst, with Northzone among its backers) and works with leading health systems such as Mount Sinai, Ochsner Health, Allina Health, and Yale New Haven.

providers.name: CoPlane
providers.description: CoPlane is a San Francisco-based enterprise software company building an AI-native intelligent operations layer for the back office of essential enterprises. The platform combines AI agents with deterministic business rules on a durable workflow engine to automate high-friction, exception-heavy processes across finance, procurement, and operations — including invoice intake, PO matching, vendor onboarding, cash application, billing, collections, bank and account reconciliation, close processes, and variance analysis. CoPlane runs inside the customer's own cloud environment and interoperates with existing enterprise systems (SAP, Workday, Coupa) across Source-to-Pay, Quote-to-Cash, and Record-to-Report workflows without a rip-and-replace migration. Founded in 2024, the company raised a $14M seed round in November 2025 led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Stripe, Optum Ventures, and Terrain. This profile was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; CoPlane does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cycle
providers.description: CYCLE (operated by CM Invest B.V., Amsterdam) is a European electric-mobility subscription service that provides e-bikes and cargo bikes to professional delivery riders, couriers, and businesses. Its all-inclusive monthly subscriptions bundle maintenance, on-site repairs, bike swaps, GPS tracking, theft protection, and remote motor control across 100+ cities in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium, Poland, Italy, and the UK. CYCLE was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the provider publishes a consumer/business marketing and operations site but exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Elevarm
providers.description: Elevarm is an upstream-focused agritech company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Bandung, Indonesia, that elevates smallholder horticulture farmers across West Java, Central Java, and Yogyakarta. It aggregates and supports more than 15,000 farmers with high-quality inputs (premium greenhouse seedlings, bio-based fertilizers, and environmentally friendly pest control via its NextBio line), lab-based soil testing through Klinik Tani, an AI-powered farming productivity app for land monitoring and data-driven agronomy recommendations, pro-farmer financing, and the PasarAgri commodity trading platform that links supply to business buyers. Elevarm is backed by Intudo, Insignia Ventures Partners, and 500 Global.

providers.name: Evigence Sensors
providers.description: Evigence Sensors is a freshness-management technology company for the food industry, combining low-cost physical sensors with data analytics to monitor food quality in real time from production to consumption at the individual item level. Its time-temperature indicator technology powers both digital (QR-scan) and visual freshness indicators applied to retail units, serving food brands, retailers, foodservice operators, cold-chain logistics providers, and consumers across the supply chain. Evigence holds 27 granted patents and its indicators meet WHO time/temperature monitoring standards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Evigence publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its verified public company properties only.

providers.name: Geek+
providers.description: Geek+ (Geekplus, HKEX: 2590) is a global leader in AI-driven autonomous mobile robot (AMR) solutions for warehouse and logistics automation. Founded in 2015, it delivers end-to-end smart-warehouse systems spanning shelf-to-person (PopPick), tote-to-person (RoboShuttle), pallet-to-person (Skycube) storage and retrieval, robot-arm picking, sorting, and intralogistics transport. Its All-in-One Software Suite (Robot Management System, Warehouse Execution System, Intelligent Warehouse Management System, data and simulation platforms) exposes open REST APIs and SDKs so customers and partners can integrate robot fleets with major WMS, ERP, and MES platforms including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Manhattan Associates, and Blue Yonder. Geek+ serves 3PL, retail, e-commerce, apparel, grocery, healthcare and pharma, manufacturing, automotive, electronics, and cold-chain logistics across 40+ countries, with 950+ deployed warehouses. In 2025 it became the world's first publicly listed AMR warehouse robotics company on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

providers.name: iMile
providers.description: iMile is a technology-driven last-mile delivery and e-commerce logistics company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Led by founder and CEO Rita Huang, iMile provides express parcel delivery, cash-on-delivery (COD), domestic and international express, dropshipping, order fulfillment, warehousing, storage, and reverse logistics / return management across more than 30 countries spanning the Middle East, China, Latin America, Africa, Europe, and Australia. The company operates its own routing, tracking, and delivery technology and employs over 20,000 people. iMile assigns each shipment a 13-digit tracking number; parcel tracking is available on imile.com and through major third-party tracking aggregators. iMile does not currently publish a first-party public developer API or open platform, so this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Keychain
providers.description: Keychain is an AI-powered operating system and network for the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industry, connecting brands and retailers with the contract manufacturers, co-packers, and suppliers that make their products. The platform lets CPG brands discover and match with vetted manufacturing partners, manage sourcing and production relationships, and streamline the supplier-discovery workflow that has traditionally been manual and relationship-driven. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Keychain was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from the a16z venture portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Keychain publishes a marketing and product web presence at keychain.com but does not expose a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API discovery surface (no developer/API subdomain, no /.well-known catalog, no llms.txt).

providers.name: Mercanis
providers.description: Mercanis is an AI-powered procurement platform that automates the end-to-end source-to-contract lifecycle for enterprise procurement teams. It combines structured intake, connected sourcing (RFx and supplier comparison), supplier relationship management, contract lifecycle management, and risk, compliance and spend analytics, coordinated by a large fleet of autonomous AI agents. Mercanis serves sectors including energy and utilities, pharma and chemicals, automotive, consumer goods, manufacturing, and construction, and integrates with ERP systems such as SAP and NetSuite alongside procurement networks like Unite. The company is headquartered in Germany with SOC-certified, GDPR-compliant infrastructure. No public developer API, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface has been identified as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Metro Africa Xpress
providers.description: Metro Africa Xpress (MAX), operating as maxdrive.ai, is a Nigerian technology-driven mobility company on a mission to make transportation safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable across Africa. MAX finances and deploys vehicles — including electric two- and three-wheelers — to a vetted network of driver-partners ("champions"), and runs a drivers services platform, electric-vehicle assembly and charging infrastructure, enterprise last-mile logistics, and mobility gov-tech solutions. Emerging from the MIT and Techstars ecosystem, MAX is backed by Novastar Ventures, Goodwell, Shell Foundation, Breakthrough Energy, Capria and Yamaha, and operates across Nigeria, Cameroon and other West African markets. The company publishes a marketing and corporate website only; no public developer program, API, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Rapido
providers.description: Rapido is an Indian on-demand urban mobility platform that connects riders with independent driver-partners (called "Captains") for bike taxis, auto rickshaws, and cabs through its consumer and Captain mobile apps. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by Accel, Rapido operates across hundreds of Indian cities and has expanded into parcel delivery and corporate mobility. As of this enrichment pass Rapido exposes only a consumer-facing web and app surface — no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification was found. This profile captures the company identity, its published policy and content pages, and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Revlon
providers.description: Revlon is a global beauty company whose portfolio spans color cosmetics, fragrance, skin care, hair color, hair care, beauty tools, and antiperspirants / deodorants. The company markets Revlon, Elizabeth Arden, Almay, Mitchum, Cutex, Charlie, SinfulColors, and Ultima II, along with a portfolio of licensed prestige and celebrity fragrance brands. Revlon Consumer Products Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the Southern District of New York on June 15, 2022 and emerged on May 2, 2023 as a privately held company controlled by its former lenders (including BrandCo noteholders such as King Street Capital, Glendon Capital, and Angelo Gordon), having cut roughly $2.7 billion of debt from its balance sheet. Today Revlon operates as a private company with reduced leverage, selling through mass-market retail and prestige channels worldwide. Revlon does not publish a public developer API; supplier, retailer, and partner integrations occur through private commercial channels (e-commerce platform integrations, EDI / GDSN feeds for retailers, and the corporate procurement portal).

providers.name: Robust.AI
providers.description: Robust.AI is a robotics company building Carter, an AI-powered collaborative mobile robot for warehouse fulfillment and manufacturing environments. Founded by Rodney Brooks (co-founder of iRobot and Rethink Robotics) and colleagues, the company designs human-centered autonomous material-handling robots that work alongside people with minimal infrastructure change, no capital expenditure, and rapid ROI. Robust.AI is backed by Playground Global and was recognized among Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies of 2026. This is a physical-robotics company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or GitHub surface.

providers.name: Saucey
providers.description: Saucey is an on-demand alcohol delivery service that brings beer, wine, and spirits from local retailers to customers' doors, often in under an hour, across a growing list of US markets. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Los Angeles, the company operates consumer iOS, Android, and web ordering experiences, a Saucey Club membership offering free delivery and perks, and a retailer/brand partnership program. Saucey is backed by 500 Global and Bullpen Capital. This profile tracks Saucey in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Saucey publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Shopeando
providers.description: Shopeando is a Mexican technology and logistics startup that manages the full international shipping process, enabling businesses and individuals to import and export merchandise between China, Europe, the United States and Mexico. Through its platform it coordinates cross-border logistics, customs handling and last-mile delivery, and provides dedicated import, export and e-commerce fulfillment services for online stores. Shopeando is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Viewlocity
providers.description: Viewlocity Technologies Pty Ltd is a supply chain management software company that provides supply chain visibility, control tower, and execution solutions for global manufacturers, distributors, and logistics providers. Its solution set spans supply chain design, inventory and asset management, supply chain management, logistics and transportation, planning and production, order lifecycle management, and supplier management, delivered as SaaS and managed services to industries including aerospace and defense, automotive and industrial, consumer goods, high tech and electronics, manufacturing, retail, and third-party logistics. Viewlocity publishes a corporate marketing and resource website but does not expose a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Zipline
providers.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan.
