The company operates a consumer mobile app and website (getmayd.com) and raised a ~EUR 30M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners in January 2022, with participation from Target Global, 468 Capital and Earlybird Venture Capital. MAYD is a consumer-facing (B2C) delivery business and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface; it is a Stripe payments customer for its checkout and billing.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: TTM Technologies
providers.description: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency components, RF microwave and microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (PCBs). TTM serves aerospace and defense, data center computing, medical, industrial and instrumentation, automotive, and networking and communications markets. The company reported approximately $2.9B in FY2025 revenue, operates 24 specialized facilities across North America and Asia Pacific, and employs more than 18,000 people. TTM expanded its defense electronics footprint with the 2022 acquisition of Telephonics from Griffon Corporation.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Airbrite
providers.description: Airbrite was an early commerce-infrastructure startup (a16z portfolio) that offered a hosted order-management and payments/commerce backend API for merchants and developers, with JavaScript and Python client SDKs and an embeddable checkout. The product was later rebranded and pivoted to "Celery" (pre-order / crowdfunding commerce). Airbrite is now defunct: its primary developer domains (airbrite.io, getairbrite.com) no longer resolve and airbrite.com is a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, API reference, or hosted API to enrich. What remains verifiable is the public github.com/airbrite organization and the client libraries still published on npm and PyPI. This profile records that residual, evidence-backed surface; most enrichment artifact types are legitimately empty because the provider no longer operates.

providers.name: Amca
providers.description: Amca (Advanced Manufacturing Company of America) is an El Segundo, California aerospace and defense manufacturer rebuilding America's industrial base by acquiring specialized component suppliers and expanding competition and capacity for critical parts — actuators, switches, hydraulics, pressure sensors, power electronics, and flight-control electronics. Founded in 2024 by Eli Giovanetti and Jai Malik, Amca combines design, testing, and production into a single RAPID platform across a network of AS9100D-certified factories (Electro-Mech Components, Electrocube, Aerospace Control Products, Payne Magnetics, Cal-Draulics, BC Power Systems), and serves nearly every major aerospace and defense prime and Tier 1 supplier — Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Textron, BAE Systems, and the Defense Logistics Agency. It is a hardware manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Autobia
providers.description: Autobia is a B2B e-commerce marketplace for the automotive aftermarket in Saudi Arabia, connecting auto-parts retailers, workshops, and service centers with wholesalers and dealers. The platform offers real-time pricing and instant ordering across more than 20,000 spare parts from multiple brands, centralizing sourcing to streamline procurement and improve supply-chain efficiency for the automotive sector. Backed by Techstars, Autobia operates via a web platform and native iOS and Android apps. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Captain Fresh
providers.description: Captain Fresh is a Bangalore, India based B2B technology company building sustainable seafood and animal-protein supply chains worldwide, connecting fishermen, farmers, processors and retailers through a technology-enabled sourcing, cold-chain and distribution marketplace. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the company operates across India and international markets. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer / supply-chain company profile; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment (a marketing website only).

providers.name: Dispatch Goods
providers.description: Dispatch Goods is a reusable-packaging and reverse-logistics company that offers returnable containers and insulated bags as an alternative to single-use and compostable packaging for direct-to-consumer meal kits, grocery delivery, and food-service operations. The company handles the full circular loop — packaging, collection, washing, and redistribution — and markets its reusable system as a cheaper and lower-impact substitute for cardboard, gel packs, and insulation, citing reductions in water use and CO2 equivalent emissions. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Haseel
providers.description: Haseel (حصيل) is a Riyadh-based technology startup, founded in 2018, that delivers fresh fruits and vegetables to consumers across Saudi Arabia through its iOS and Android mobile apps. The company sources high-quality produce and fulfills each order from the nearest of its branches inside Riyadh, pairing a curated selection with fast, reliable last-mile delivery. Haseel reports more than 400,000 app downloads, three branches inside Riyadh, and over 1,000 orders per day, and is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Haseel is a consumer produce-delivery app and does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Otrafy
providers.description: Otrafy is an AI-powered supplier management platform that automates regulatory compliance, supplier data collection, and supply chain risk assessment for QA, R&D, Regulatory, and Procurement teams at enterprise clients. The platform uses natural language processing to automate supplier data collection (citing high supplier response rates), monitors suppliers in real time against regulatory standards such as FDA, EU MRLs, California Prop 65, and PFAS, and applies AI-driven risk scoring to suppliers and facilities to streamline buyer-supplier collaboration. Otrafy is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website and product/contact pages but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: B2B-Center
providers.description: B2B-Center is one of Russia's largest electronic trading platforms (ETP) for business-to-business procurement, operating at b2b-center.ru. The platform hosts electronic tenders, auctions, and competitive sourcing procedures that connect corporate and commercial buyers with a broad network of suppliers across many industries. It provides tools for organizing purchases, publishing procurement notices, qualifying and managing suppliers, and running the full electronic bidding lifecycle. B2B-Center is backed by Insight Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company awaiting deeper enrichment.

providers.name: Phillips 66
providers.description: Phillips 66 is a diversified energy manufacturing and logistics company with midstream, chemicals, refining, and marketing and specialties businesses. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for Phillips 66.

providers.name: 6river
providers.description: 6 River Systems (6RS) is a warehouse fulfillment automation company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts. Its flagship product is "Chuck," a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AMR) that works alongside human associates to guide and optimize picking, sorting, and replenishment in distribution centers. The platform is WMS-agnostic and integrates with existing warehouse-management systems as an intelligent execution layer via a private/partner REST API for host data exchange; it does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or consumer SDKs. Norwest Venture Partners was an early investor; the company was acquired by Shopify in 2019 and by Ocado Group in 2023. The public marketing site at 6river.com currently serves a parked lander stub.

providers.name: AVO
providers.description: Avo (avonow.com) was a New York City-based "building commerce" and workplace-amenity platform, founded 2017-2018 out of Y Combinator (S18) and backed by Insight Partners and Kleiner Perkins with roughly $84M raised. It offered white-labeled same-day delivery of groceries, household goods, alcohol and personal-care items into residential and office buildings with no order minimums or delivery fees, plus on-site and virtual event programming and corporate gifting and recognition services, serving apartment communities, corporations, hospitals and universities across New York, New Jersey, Chicago and Houston. Avo published no API, SDK or developer portal, and as of a 2026-07-20 probe its domain resolves to a parked lander with no operational hosts; Y Combinator lists the company as inactive.

providers.name: Baan
providers.description: Baan (Baan Company N.V., originally The Baan Corporation) was a Dutch enterprise resource planning software vendor founded in 1978 in Barneveld, Netherlands by Jan Baan and later joined by his brother Paul Baan. Baan built one of the first genuinely component-based ERP suites, known for its Dynamic Enterprise Modeler (DEM), its Baan Tools 4GL development environment, and deep manufacturing and project-industry functionality. At its late-1990s peak Baan served roughly 3,000 customers and posted close to $700 million in revenue, making it one of the leading global ERP providers alongside SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft. Following accounting controversy and a collapse in its share price, Baan was acquired by the British engineering group Invensys in 2000, sold on to SSA Global Technologies in 2003, and absorbed into Infor Global Solutions when Infor acquired SSA in 2006. Baan no longer exists as an operating company or an independent brand: the product line lives on as Infor LN, and the baan.com and baan.nl domains now permanently redirect to the Infor LN product page. Consequently this profile carries no first-party API surface of its own — any modern programmatic access to the Baan lineage is delivered through Infor LN REST APIs and the Infor ION API gateway on Infor's developer platform. Baan Company is listed by Battery Ventures as an exited investment.

providers.name: Benchmark Electronics
providers.description: Benchmark Electronics, Inc. is an advanced electronics engineering and manufacturing services (EMS) company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. The company provides integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing services from prototypes to high-volume production, including procurement, logistics, and repair. Benchmark serves original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical technologies, commercial aerospace, industrial, next-gen communications, advanced computing, and semiconductor capital equipment markets. The company operates approximately 22 locations in 8 countries with around 13,000 employees.

providers.name: Chefs' Warehouse
providers.description: The Chefs' Warehouse, Inc. (NASDAQ: CHEF) is a premier distributor of specialty food products to high-end independent restaurants, fine dining establishments, country clubs, hotels, caterers, culinary schools, bakeries, and specialty food stores across North America and the Middle East. The company offers a broad portfolio of artisan, exotic, and signature ingredients spanning center-of-the-plate proteins, specialty dry goods, produce, pastry, cheese and charcuterie, dairy and eggs, oils and vinegars, and kitchen supplies. Customers order through a B2B e-commerce platform (re-platformed to Optimizely B2B in 2021, previously Magento) and companion iOS and Android wholesale-ordering apps built in partnership with Unbound Commerce. As of this profiling, Chefs' Warehouse does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or open-source repositories; its digital surface is a buyer-facing ordering experience rather than a programmatic API. This profile documents the company's public footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cornershop by Uber
providers.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

providers.name: Embark Trucks
providers.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.
